cuts.notes: Labouré College of Healthcare (founded 1892, 134 years) will cease all academic operations August 31, 2026. Board of Directors unanimously approved merger/acquisition agreement with Curry College (~4 miles away in Milton, MA). Nursing programs will transfer to Curry's School of Nursing and Health Sciences under a new unit called the Labouré Center for Advancing Healthcare Opportunity. Reasons cited: persistent financial and enrollment challenges, and regulatory hurdles (state regulators voted to shut down nursing program in 2023 after students failed 80% first-time NCLEX pass rate threshold; decision overturned on appeal; scores restored to full approval by May 2024). Enrollment declined from peak of 1,188 (fall 2020) to 530 (fall 2024), roughly a 55% drop. Only 168 new students enrolled in 2025 vs. goal of 300. ASN nursing students (majority of enrollment) will transfer to Curry's Milton campus in fall 2026; tuition and fees held at 2026-2027 Labouré rates; credits transfer seamlessly. Students in other programs (e.g. respiratory care) being directed to articulation agreements at other institutions if unable to complete by Aug. 31. Curry plans to hire ~15 Labouré nursing faculty and ~20 staff (35-40 total of ~100 total Labouré employees). As of Nov. 1, 2024: 23 FT instructional employees, 49 noninstructional staff at Labouré. Labouré endowment pledged to support the new Center. Labouré plans to sell its physical property (303 Adams St, Milton — former Aquinas College campus) and use proceeds to fund the Center. Curry enrolled ~2,000 students in fall 2024 and also faced enrollment declines; acquisition expected to potentially double Curry nursing enrollment. Deal subject to regulatory approval at time of announcement.
